correctness.rationale: Closed neighborhoods have size seven, so even two centers cannot cover sixteen vertices. Independently covering all vertex triples by direct set unions gives exactly 32; for an anchored pair, the uncovered-set test gives zero extensions for all differences in A or the order-two class and exactly the two stated extensions for each difference in B. In particular {(0,0),(1,2),(2,1)} covers all vertices and contradicts the cited ordinary gamma=4 claim for the standard graph. To check the geometric identification independently, use the 32 periodic square triangles {p,p+(1,1),p+e_i} (i=1,2); the given determinant-one map L takes their full set exactly to the computed minimum family. The inverse map identifies the complex with the triangulation of R²/(4Z)²: every allowed adjacency triangle lifts about a vertex, since the six neighbor differences have coordinates in {−1,0,1} and no difference between two of these offsets wraps into an allowed step. The link is the planar six-cycle, so there are no larger cliques or extraneous quotient triangles. Direct membership traces on every support of size at most three verify that precisely their subfaces are shattered, consistent with the two translated witness tables; larger supports cannot realize the all-positive trace. The same positive-branch requirement bounds online depth by three since a consistent full tree cannot repeat a query on a branch, and a shattered triple attains three. Integral reduced homology follows from the explicit torus, not from the modular rank in the supplied checks.
residual_risks: Exact for standard closed-neighborhood domination and the specified Cayley graph. The numerical modular check alone would not prove integral torsion-freeness.

value.rationale: This is an exact structural link between a canonical finite optimization family and a topology-bearing complexity invariant, not just two previously recoverable counts. Co-occurrence of an optimal pair reconstructs a disjoint isomorphic Cayley graph, and the otherwise stronger requirement of every membership trace happens to recover exactly that graph's clique complex. Its integral torus topology is substantially more informative than the VC dimension or a modular rank and permits a precise comparison with the matching rook parameters and different concept families.
residual_risks: The value is for this natural graph and comparison family; not a general result for strongly regular graphs.
